findings.issue_text: Duplicate `def self.downsize` definition in optimized_image.rb — the second 3-arg definition silently shadows the first 4-arg version, breaking existing callers with TypeError/NoMethodError and crashing thumbnail generation

`optimize`'s new contract passes a pre-formatted dimensions string into `*_instructions` methods (resize_instructions, downsize_instructions, and animated variants) that were written against the old width/height convention, so the convert command is assembled incorrectly or raises

GIF detection in `optimize` tests `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` against the tempfile path which has no .gif extension, so the animated-vs-static instruction dispatch can never select the animated path for the uploads_controller caller

Animated GIFs uploaded over the size limit get downsized with static-image instructions, which either fails (burning all 5 retry attempts silently) or strips animation, making the promised 'allow users to upload large animated images' behavior unreachable

downsize failure is unhandled in uploads_controller.rb:65–67 — `convert_with` returns false on non-zero exit but the loop ignores it and decrements attempt, re-running the same failing command 4 more times (5 wasted convert spawns per upload attempt) then silently proceeding with the original oversized tempfile

Client-side `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` in utilities.js:182 hardcodes the cap while the server enforces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so client and server checks disagree — e.g. a 15MB image on a site with max_image_size_kb = 20480 is rejected client-side with a wrong error message
uploads_controller.rb passes '80%' as dimensions to OptimizedImage.downsize, but the new API contract expects a 'WxH' string, causing parse failure and a generic 500 error
The downsize loop is hard-capped at 5 iterations of 80% scale, so images much larger than max_image_size_kb still fail with the original 'file too large' error the feature was meant to eliminate
No spec verifies large-image upload succeeds for any size, and none could pass at these bounds

utilities.js replaces the per-type site setting with a hardcoded 10MB limit for all upload types, breaking admin-configured limits for non-image attachments and mismatching server enforcement for images
Non-image types now bypass max_attachment_size_kb client-side with no replacement enforcement anywhere in the diff

optimized_image.rb changes resize/downsize signature to a combined dimensions string, but all other existing call sites still pass separate width/height integers, breaking thumbnails and avatars across the app
No caller audit or tests are included for the OptimizedImage API rewrite
allow_animation flag is passed but the animated branch only fires on .GIF filenames, which tempfile.path never ends with, so animated GIFs are silently flattened or not downsized
Second def self.downsize definition is a duplicate that makes the first definition dead code
In-place downsize mutates the uploaded tempfile but content_type and filename are left unchanged, so upload record metadata may no longer match the bytes
No test files appear anywhere in the diff despite new non-trivial behavior in the controller loop and OptimizedImage API rewrite
Downsize loop does not enforce the invariant: 5 iterations of 80% pixel scaling may leave file size above max_image_size_kb, so oversized uploads still reach the user via Upload.create_for
Downsize rewrites tempfile.path in place (from == to), which ImageMagick does not reliably support and can truncate/zero the file, then Upload.create_for uses the stale original tempfile.size

Public downsize signature in optimized_image.rb changed from (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) to (from, to, dimensions, opts), breaking existing callers like thumbnail generation and pull_hotlinked_images
downsize is defined twice in the same class; the second def silently replaces the first, leaving dead code that will mislead future edits
utilities.js hardcodes client-side max-size checks to 10 * 1024 KB instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, breaking sites with raised or lowered limits
uploads_controller.rb API URL-download path hardcodes 10.megabytes in FileHelper.download, ignoring SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and silently returning nil via rescue nil
allow_animation reuses SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails (a thumbnail setting) to gate animation of the original upload during downsizing
Animated GIF path is dead: optimize selects _animated instructions only for .GIF extensions, but Rails tempfile paths have no extension, so animated GIFs always use static first-frame instructions
No test coverage for the new downsize loop in the diff

Duplicate definition of self.downsize in optimized_image.rb — second definition silently replaces the first, breaking all existing 4-argument callers (dimensions binds an Integer, opts becomes an Integer, TypeError on opts[:allow_animation], and geometry string becomes width-only, changing resize semantics)

uploads_controller.rb passes '80%' as dimensions but downsize_instructions expects a WxH geometry string, producing malformed instructions; combined with the 5-attempt cap, large images can exit the loop still over max_image_size_kb and silently fail with no error to the user
OptimizedImage.downsize uses the same tempfile path for input and output, which is unsupported by ImageMagick and can corrupt/truncate the output; should write to a fresh temp file

utilities.js hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 client-side for all upload types, ignoring SiteSetting max_attachment_size_kb/max_avatar_size_kb, blocking uploads over 10MB and forking the site setting into a hardcoded constant (also hardcoded server-side in FileHelper.download)

Animated-GIF detection in optimize keys off the file extension via regex, but tempfiles have no .gif extension, so allow_animated_thumbnails never applies and animated GIFs are silently flattened to their first frame; should use content-type detection

Downsize loop runs up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick shell-outs inline in the request cycle with no timeout, blocking unicorn workers and risking worker starvation under bursts of large uploads; image work should be in background jobs

utilities.js:182 and :246 — configurable max_image_size_kb site setting silently replaced with hardcoded 10MB constant, decoupling client validation and 413 error messages from admin-configured setting
uploads_controller.rb:55 — API/URL download path replaces max_image_size_kb enforcement with fixed 10.megabytes download cap, changing bandwidth/memory exposure per API request

uploads_controller.rb:63-69 — server now downsizes and accepts oversized uploads but client-side rejection logic is retained, leaving contradictory intents where browser users get rejection messages for files the server would downsize
optimized_image.rb:142-145 vs 148-150 — downsize defined twice in same module; second definition overwrites the first, breaking existing callers passing width/height as two arguments
uploads_controller.rb:66 — OptimizedImage.downsize reuses the original tempfile as both source and destination, destructively overwriting the user's original upload

Server-side size limit silently converted from hard rejection to downsize-then-accept, with the hard cap only 10MB for the API-URL path and unbounded for the normal file-upload path, allowing authenticated users to upload arbitrarily large files and trigger up to 5 ImageMagick convert passes (resource-exhaustion/DoS vector)

Client-side upload limit hardcoded to 10 * 1024 KB in utilities.js, discarding Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], causing false 'file too large' rejections on sites with limits above 10MB and missed early errors on sites with small limits

Downsize gating in uploads_controller.rb relies on FileHelper.is_image?(filename) using the user-controlled filename/extension rather than file content, allowing non-image files named .png to be processed through up to 5 ImageMagick passes and real images with mismatched extensions to skip downsizing
optimized_image.rb: downsize defined twice, second definition silently shadows the first so the 4-arg form raises ArgumentError, with no spec updates for the changed downsize/resize signatures
optimized_image.rb: public signatures of downsize/resize changed from (width, height) to a single dimensions string with zero spec updates
uploads_controller.rb: new retry loop (attempt = 5; while attempt > 0 && ...) is new behavior with no controller/request spec
utilities.js: client-side size check changed from site-setting to hardcoded 10 MB with no JS spec changes

uploads_controller.rb:63-69: downsize loop ignores the false return value of OptimizedImage.downsize when the convert shell command fails, retrying the unchanged file 5 times before falling through to Upload.create_for with an over-limit tempfile, yielding 5 wasted converts and a generic upload failure instead of a downsize failure
Duplicate method definition of OptimizedImage.downsize shadows the first definition, causing existing 4-arg callers to silently discard the height argument and produce wrong-sized images
In-place downsize loop overwrites the user's original upload with no backup, potentially permanently destroying the only copy of the uploaded file if conversion fails partway
No lower bound on the downsize loop: tempfile.size can stay above max_image_size_kb after 5 attempts and Upload.create_for still runs, failing size validation after destroying the original
Client-side 413 cap hardcodes 10MB in utilities.js, desynchronizing from the server's max_image_size_kb setting, causing silent rejection of allowed images or acceptance of files the server rejects
FileHelper.is_image?(filename) misclassifies when filename is a URL basename
Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored in uploads_controller.rb:63-69, so failed downsizes are silently swallowed with no logging of ImageMagick failures
downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) uses the same path for input and output, causing ImageMagick to fail or produce a corrupted image that is persisted as the upload
Client-side hardcoded 10 * 1024 limit in utilities.js:182 desyncs from server-side SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, causing 413 errors reporting the wrong limit
Fixed 5-iteration loop with blind '80%' shrink cannot downsize very large images below max_image_size_kb, causing deterministic rejection of the largest files

Animated-GIF branch in optimized_image.rb is keyed on '.GIF' filename extension, but controller passes tempfile.path with no extension, so animated GIFs are silently flattened to a single frame and allow_animation is dead code
downsize is defined twice in the same module body in optimized_image.rb:139-152, with the second definition silently overriding the first
FileHelper.is_image?(filename) gates downsizing on a filename that may lack an extension for API-URL uploads, silently skipping downsizing for those files with no distinguishing log

This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate `def self.downsize` definition in optimized_image.rb — the second 3-arg definition silently shadows the first 4-arg version, breaking existing callers with TypeError/NoMethodError and crashing thumbnail generation

`optimize`'s new contract passes a pre-formatted dimensions string into `*_instructions` methods (resize_instructions, downsize_instructions, and animated variants) that were written against the old width/height convention, so the convert command is assembled incorrectly or raises

adjudication.rationale: In the pre-change code, `optimize(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` immediately converted `width,height` into a single dimensions string via `dimensions(width, height)` and then passed that string into `*_instructions` (`self.send(method_name, from, to, dim, opts)`). After the change, `optimize` is explicitly passed a dimensions string and still forwards it to `*_instructions` in the same way. So the finding’s claim that instruction methods were written for a width/height convention and will now assemble the convert command incorrectly is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GIF detection in `optimize` tests `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` against the tempfile path which has no .gif extension, so the animated-vs-static instruction dispatch can never select the animated path for the uploads_controller caller

adjudication.rationale: `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects animated instructions only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. This diff adds a new call site in `UploadsController#create_upload` that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ..., allow_animation: ...)` on a `Tempfile` path. The tempfiles created here (notably via `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`) are not shown to preserve the original `.gif` extension, so the regex check can fail even when `filename` is a GIF (the controller separately uses `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` based on the original name). That means the animated path may never be chosen for this new downsizing flow, breaking intended handling of animated GIFs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Animated GIFs uploaded over the size limit get downsized with static-image instructions, which either fails (burning all 5 retry attempts silently) or strips animation, making the promised 'allow users to upload large animated images' behavior unreachable

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, oversized images are downsized via `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated-path is selected only if `opts[:allow_animation]` is true **and** `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Here `from` is `tempfile.path`, which typically has no `.gif` extension, so even for an uploaded animated GIF the `_animated` instructions won’t be used. That means animated GIFs will be processed with the static instructions, likely stripping animation or failing to reduce size, making the intended behavior unreachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: downsize failure is unhandled in uploads_controller.rb:65–67 — `convert_with` returns false on non-zero exit but the loop ignores it and decrements attempt, re-running the same failing command 4 more times (5 wasted convert spawns per upload attempt) then silently proceeding with the original oversized tempfile

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but never checks its return value. In optimized_image.rb, `convert_with` returns `false` on non-zero exit and `optimize` returns that result, so `downsize` can fail. If it fails, `tempfile.size` will remain unchanged, the loop condition (`tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`) will stay true, and the code will retry up to 5 times while blindly decrementing `attempt`, then proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` without surfacing an error or guaranteeing the file is within limits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` in utilities.js:182 hardcodes the cap while the server enforces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so client and server checks disagree — e.g. a 15MB image on a site with max_image_size_kb = 20480 is rejected client-side with a wrong error message
uploads_controller.rb passes '80%' as dimensions to OptimizedImage.downsize, but the new API contract expects a 'WxH' string, causing parse failure and a generic 500 error

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `OptimizedImage.downsize` to accept a single `dimensions` argument (and forwards it directly to `*_instructions`). In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new call `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", allow_animation: ...)` matches that new signature. The diff does not show any parsing/validation that requires a strict `"WxH"` format, and ImageMagick-style geometry strings like `"80%"` are commonly valid; therefore the claimed parse failure and resulting 500 cannot be verified from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The downsize loop is hard-capped at 5 iterations of 80% scale, so images much larger than max_image_size_kb still fail with the original 'file too large' error the feature was meant to eliminate

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new logic only retries downsizing a maximum of 5 times (`attempt = 5` and `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`), each time calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`. That guarantees at most 5 passes of reduction; if the file still exceeds `max_image_size_kb` after those passes, the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` with an oversized `tempfile.size`, so the upload can still be rejected as too large. This is a real limitation/edge case of the new feature, but it’s not a strictly verifiable “always broken” defect from the diff alone (it depends on input sizes/compressibility).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec verifies large-image upload succeeds for any size, and none could pass at these bounds

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior to downsize oversized image uploads (uploads_controller.rb loop calling OptimizedImage.downsize) and changes size limits to a 10MB constant, but it does not show any spec files. From this diff alone you cannot verify that “no spec verifies large-image upload succeeds” across the codebase, nor that “none could pass at these bounds”; those claims depend on tests not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: utilities.js replaces the per-type site setting with a hardcoded 10MB limit for all upload types, breaking admin-configured limits for non-image attachments and mismatching server enforcement for images
Non-image types now bypass max_attachment_size_kb client-side with no replacement enforcement anywhere in the diff

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the client-side size check was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This means uploads of non-image types (e.g. attachments) no longer honor their configured max (e.g. `max_attachment_size_kb`) on the client. The only new server-side logic in the diff is image-specific downsizing in `uploads_controller.rb` gated by `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, so there is no replacement enforcement for non-image types shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: optimized_image.rb changes resize/downsize signature to a combined dimensions string, but all other existing call sites still pass separate width/height integers, breaking thumbnails and avatars across the app

adjudication.rationale: In optimized_image.rb, `downsize` is defined twice: first as `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then redefined as `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, so the latter overrides the former in Ruby. This diff therefore removes the old 4-arg API unless all call sites were updated; only one call site in this diff (uploads_controller.rb) is shown updated to pass a single dimensions string ("80%"). The finding’s claim that “all other existing call sites still pass separate width/height” isn’t verifiable from the provided diff, but the API-breaking redefinition is a concrete risk created here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No caller audit or tests are included for the OptimizedImage API rewrite

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites the OptimizedImage API (e.g., `resize` now passes a single "#{width}x#{height}" string, `optimize` signature changes from `(width, height)` to `(dimensions)`, and a new `downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts)` is introduced). This is a nontrivial interface change that can impact existing callers beyond the one new usage in `uploads_controller.rb`, yet the diff shows no accompanying tests or any explicit verification/audit of other call sites in the codebase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: allow_animation flag is passed but the animated branch only fires on .GIF filenames, which tempfile.path never ends with, so animated GIFs are silently flattened or not downsized

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, downsizing is invoked as `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated code path is selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true **and** `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Here, `from` is `tempfile.path` (a generated temp filename that typically lacks the original `.gif` extension), while the original `filename` (which would end in `.gif`) is not used for that check. This means animated GIF uploads can miss the `_animated` instructions branch even when `allow_animation` is enabled, leading to incorrect processing of animated GIFs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Second def self.downsize definition is a duplicate that makes the first definition dead code

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/optimized_image.rb the diff defines `def self.downsize` twice: first with signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then again with `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby does not overload methods by arity, so the second definition overwrites the first, making the first effectively dead code and changing behavior for callers that pass 4 args.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In-place downsize mutates the uploaded tempfile but content_type and filename are left unchanged, so upload record metadata may no longer match the bytes

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an in-place downsize loop on `tempfile.path`, but it still passes the same `filename` and `content_type` into `Upload.create_for`. From what’s shown, `OptimizedImage.downsize` writes back to the same path (same extension/filename), and the size used for the upload record is taken after downsizing (`tempfile.size` at `Upload.create_for` call). The finding’s claim that the metadata will “no longer match the bytes” (due to unchanged filename/content_type) isn’t verifiable from the diff, since there’s no evidence the downsize changes file format/MIME type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test files appear anywhere in the diff despite new non-trivial behavior in the controller loop and OptimizedImage API rewrite

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces non-trivial new behavior (a loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that repeatedly downsizes images up to 5 times based on `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, and a refactor/overload of `OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize` method signatures). No spec/test files are added or modified anywhere in the shown diff, so the finding about missing tests for these changes is diff-grounded and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize loop does not enforce the invariant: 5 iterations of 80% pixel scaling may leave file size above max_image_size_kb, so oversized uploads still reach the user via Upload.create_for

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing logic in `UploadsController#create_upload` only tries up to 5 iterations of `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%")` while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, but it does not enforce (or even check after the loop) that the final `tempfile.size` is now under the limit before calling `Upload.create_for(...)`. From the diff alone we can verify the loop can exit with `attempt == 0` while still oversized; whether that results in an accepted oversized upload depends on `Upload.create_for` validations (not shown), so the finding’s “still reach the user” claim isn’t provable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize rewrites tempfile.path in place (from == to), which ImageMagick does not reliably support and can truncate/zero the file, then Upload.create_for uses the stale original tempfile.size
matched_golden_ids: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to `tempfile.size` being stale/cached after the file is modified, causing logic based on size checks to behave incorrectly (golden emphasizes non-terminating loop; candidate emphasizes stale size after in-place rewrite). The core issue—relying on an outdated `tempfile.size` after modifications—is the same.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public downsize signature in optimized_image.rb changed from (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) to (from, to, dimensions, opts), breaking existing callers like thumbnail generation and pull_hotlinked_images

adjudication.rationale: In optimized_image.rb, `self.downsize` is redefined: it first accepts `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` but later a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` overrides it. The effective public signature becomes `(from, to, dimensions, opts)`, so any existing callers still passing width/height as separate args would raise an argument error at runtime. The diff itself shows this breaking redefinition, though the specific external callers named aren’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: downsize is defined twice in the same class; the second def silently replaces the first, leaving dead code that will mislead future edits

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/optimized_image.rb the method `self.downsize` is defined twice: first as `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then again (later in the file) as `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the second definition overrides the first, making the earlier implementation dead/unreachable and potentially breaking any callers that still pass 4 args (max_width, max_height). This is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: utilities.js hardcodes client-side max-size checks to 10 * 1024 KB instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, breaking sites with raised or lowered limits

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly replaces the client-side max-size check in `utilities.js` from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) in both the generic file-size check and the 413 error handler. This will cause incorrect client-side validation/messaging on sites whose configured upload limits differ from 10MB, so the finding is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: uploads_controller.rb API URL-download path hardcodes 10.megabytes in FileHelper.download, ignoring SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and silently returning nil via rescue nil

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the API URL download limit from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` (`tempfile = FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) rescue nil`), so it does ignore the site setting for that specific download cap. However, this isn’t necessarily a correctness bug on its own (it may be intentional to allow downloading larger images for later downsizing), and the `rescue nil` behavior was already present before the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: allow_animation reuses SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails (a thumbnail setting) to gate animation of the original upload during downsizing

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb, the new downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`, which ties whether animated uploads are processed as animated during downsizing to a setting named for thumbnails. The finding correctly points out this reuse/mismatch; it’s a specific design/configuration concern introduced by the diff, though not provably a functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Animated GIF path is dead: optimize selects _animated instructions only for .GIF extensions, but Rails tempfile paths have no extension, so animated GIFs always use static first-frame instructions

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, animated instructions are selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is truthy **and** `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. The new upload logic in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`, passing the **tempfile path** as `from`. Tempfile paths commonly lack the original `.gif` extension, so the regex check won’t match and `_animated` instructions won’t be used, causing animated GIFs to be processed with the non-animated (first-frame) path despite `allow_animation` being set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for the new downsize loop in the diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new nontrivial behavior in `UploadsController#create_upload` (a retry loop that repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` until `tempfile.size` is under `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, up to 5 attempts). This change affects upload handling and image processing, but the PR diff contains no corresponding test additions/updates covering this new loop or its edge cases (e.g., non-shrinking images, animated thumbnails option, max attempts).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate definition of self.downsize in optimized_image.rb — second definition silently replaces the first, breaking all existing 4-argument callers (dimensions binds an Integer, opts becomes an Integer, TypeError on opts[:allow_animation], and geometry string becomes width-only, changing resize semantics)

uploads_controller.rb passes '80%' as dimensions but downsize_instructions expects a WxH geometry string, producing malformed instructions; combined with the 5-attempt cap, large images can exit the loop still over max_image_size_kb and silently fail with no error to the user

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UploadsController` calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` after `OptimizedImage.downsize` was (re)defined to accept a single `dimensions` string. Nothing in the diff shows that `downsize_instructions` rejects percent geometry; in ImageMagick-style tooling, `80%` is commonly a valid resize geometry, so “malformed instructions” is not verifiable from the change. Additionally, the claim that the loop can end still oversized and then “silently fail with no error to the user” isn’t supported by the diff, since the post-loop behavior/error handling isn’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OptimizedImage.downsize uses the same tempfile path for input and output, which is unsupported by ImageMagick and can corrupt/truncate the output; should write to a fresh temp file

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, passing the same path for both `from` and `to`. In `optimized_image.rb`, `downsize` ultimately shells out via `convert_with(instructions, to)`, i.e., it asks the external ImageMagick command to write the output to `to`. With `from == to`, this performs an in-place rewrite via the external tool, which can lead to corruption/truncation or failure during conversion; the diff does not introduce any safeguard (like writing to a separate temp file and atomically replacing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: utilities.js hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 client-side for all upload types, ignoring SiteSetting max_attachment_size_kb/max_avatar_size_kb, blocking uploads over 10MB and forking the site setting into a hardcoded constant (also hardcoded server-side in FileHelper.download)

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces dynamic site-setting limits with hardcoded 10MB constants. In `utilities.js`, `maxSizeKB` is changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to `10 * 1024`, so all client-side upload checks ignore per-type settings (attachments/avatars/images) and will block uploads >10MB even if settings allow larger. Similarly, in `uploads_controller.rb` the API URL download limit changes from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to `10.megabytes`, also ignoring configuration. This is a concrete behavior/config regression shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Animated-GIF detection in optimize keys off the file extension via regex, but tempfiles have no .gif extension, so allow_animated_thumbnails never applies and animated GIFs are silently flattened to their first frame; should use content-type detection

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, animated handling is selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true **and** `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` (file-extension regex). This PR adds an upload-time loop that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` in `UploadsController#create_upload`. Here `from` is `tempfile.path`, which (especially for the URL-download case `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`) is very likely a temp filename without a `.gif` suffix. That means the `_animated` instructions won’t be used even when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled, so animated GIFs can be processed with non-animated conversion logic (risking flattening).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize loop runs up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick shell-outs inline in the request cycle with no timeout, blocking unicorn workers and risking worker starvation under bursts of large uploads; image work should be in background jobs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an inline loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that can run up to 5 iterations of `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` while the request is being handled. `OptimizedImage` executes ImageMagick via backticks in `convert_with` (shell-out) with no timeout/kill mechanism shown. This can block the web worker during large uploads and is a performance/architecture risk (potential worker starvation under load), but it’s not a directly verifiable functional correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: utilities.js:182 and :246 — configurable max_image_size_kb site setting silently replaced with hardcoded 10MB constant, decoupling client validation and 413 error messages from admin-configured setting

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly replaces site-setting-based limits with hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB in `utilities.js` (both the generic `max_' + type + '_size_kb` lookup and the 413 handler’s `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`). This demonstrably decouples client-side size validation and the displayed “file too large” max from admin-configured settings. Whether it’s an intentional product change (e.g., allowing larger images to be downsized server-side) isn’t provable from the diff alone, but the finding about the replacement/mismatch is accurate and review-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: uploads_controller.rb:55 — API/URL download path replaces max_image_size_kb enforcement with fixed 10.megabytes download cap, changing bandwidth/memory exposure per API request

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the API URL download cap from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a fixed `10.megabytes` (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). This verifiably removes the site-configured limit from the download step, potentially allowing larger-than-configured downloads (increasing bandwidth/memory exposure) and also potentially rejecting expected larger downloads when the setting is >10MB. The later downsizing loop only runs after the download completes, so it does not mitigate the resource exposure during download.

adjudication_records.issue_text: uploads_controller.rb:63-69 — server now downsizes and accepts oversized uploads but client-side rejection logic is retained, leaving contradictory intents where browser users get rejection messages for files the server would downsize

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds server-side logic in uploads_controller.rb to accept an image tempfile and repeatedly downsize it until it is <= SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb (lines added around 60-69). However, the client-side upload size check in utilities.js still rejects files based on maxSizeKB, now hardcoded to 10*1024 (10MB), before the upload is attempted. This means browser uploads over the client threshold will be blocked even though the server now intends to handle oversized images by downsizing, creating inconsistent behavior and preventing the new server-side capability from being used via the browser.

adjudication_records.issue_text: optimized_image.rb:142-145 vs 148-150 — downsize defined twice in same module; second definition overwrites the first, breaking existing callers passing width/height as two arguments

adjudication_records.issue_text: uploads_controller.rb:66 — OptimizedImage.downsize reuses the original tempfile as both source and destination, destructively overwriting the user's original upload

adjudication.rationale: The new code intentionally downsizes the upload before creating the Upload record, calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` to mutate the server-side tempfile. Nothing in the diff shows that preserving the pre-downsized tempfile is required, nor that in-place conversion is incorrect; the stated issue about "overwriting the user's original upload" isn’t substantiated by the diff (the user’s local file isn’t affected).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side size limit silently converted from hard rejection to downsize-then-accept, with the hard cap only 10MB for the API-URL path and unbounded for the normal file-upload path, allowing authenticated users to upload arbitrarily large files and trigger up to 5 ImageMagick convert passes (resource-exhaustion/DoS vector)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce new server-side behavior that can increase resource usage: in `uploads_controller.rb`, large image tempfiles are processed in a loop up to 5 times via `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` before `Upload.create_for(...)` runs, meaning expensive ImageMagick work can occur even if the upload would ultimately be rejected later (limits/validation not shown in this diff). Also, the API-URL download cap is changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a fixed `10.megabytes`. However, the finding’s stronger claim that normal file uploads are now “unbounded” / allow “arbitrarily large files” is not verifiable from the diff alone (server/web-tier/request limits and `Upload.create_for` validations are outside the shown changes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side upload limit hardcoded to 10 * 1024 KB in utilities.js, discarding Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], causing false 'file too large' rejections on sites with limits above 10MB and missed early errors on sites with small limits
matched_golden_ids: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize gating in uploads_controller.rb relies on FileHelper.is_image?(filename) using the user-controlled filename/extension rather than file content, allowing non-image files named .png to be processed through up to 5 ImageMagick passes and real images with mismatched extensions to skip downsizing

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing block in `uploads_controller.rb` gates ImageMagick processing on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, and the diff shows `filename` comes from `File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)` or `file.original_filename` (both user-controlled). That means the decision to run up to 5 `OptimizedImage.downsize` passes is based on the name, not the actual tempfile/content. The specific claim that `is_image?` is extension-based and that mismatched extensions will skip downsizing is plausible but not provable from this diff alone, so this is a real diff-grounded concern about robustness/perf/security rather than a fully verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: optimized_image.rb: downsize defined twice, second definition silently shadows the first so the 4-arg form raises ArgumentError, with no spec updates for the changed downsize/resize signatures

adjudication.rationale: In `optimized_image.rb` the diff leaves an existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then adds a new later `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the later method definition overrides the earlier one, so any existing callers using the 4-arg (width/height) form will now hit an `ArgumentError` due to the signature change. This shadowing is directly visible in the diff. The claim about missing spec updates isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the duplicate/overridden method is a concrete defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: optimized_image.rb: public signatures of downsize/resize changed from (width, height) to a single dimensions string with zero spec updates

adjudication.rationale: In `optimized_image.rb`, `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is effectively replaced by a later redefinition `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, which changes the public method signature to take a single `dimensions` argument. The diff shows no corresponding spec/test updates (no spec files touched) and only one new call site updated (`OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`), so this API change risks unupdated callers/tests outside the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: uploads_controller.rb: new retry loop (attempt = 5; while attempt > 0 && ...) is new behavior with no controller/request spec

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial behavior in `uploads_controller.rb`: a retry loop that conditionally downsizes uploaded images in-place up to 5 times (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes ... OptimizedImage.downsize(...)`). This change affects upload handling and would typically warrant request/controller coverage to ensure correct outcomes (e.g., stops at limit, preserves animations per setting, handles failures). However, the claim that there is "no controller/request spec" cannot be verified from the diff alone (no test files are shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: utilities.js: client-side size check changed from site-setting to hardcoded 10 MB with no JS spec changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the client-side max upload size checks were changed from site settings (`Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`) to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB (10MB). This removes configurability and can cause incorrect behavior (e.g., blocking uploads >10MB even if the site setting allows larger, or mismatching server-side limits/settings), making it a real, user-visible regression introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: uploads_controller.rb:63-69: downsize loop ignores the false return value of OptimizedImage.downsize when the convert shell command fails, retrying the unchanged file 5 times before falling through to Upload.create_for with an over-limit tempfile, yielding 5 wasted converts and a generic upload failure instead of a downsize failure

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new loop repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but never checks its return value (lines added around 63-69). In optimized_image.rb, `optimize` returns `convert_with(...)`, and `convert_with` explicitly returns `false` when the shell convert command fails (`return false if $?.exitstatus != 0`). If downsizing fails, `tempfile.size` will remain unchanged, so the loop will retry up to 5 times doing no effective work, then proceed to `Upload.create_for` potentially still over the configured limit, yielding a generic upload failure rather than handling the downsize failure explicitly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate method definition of OptimizedImage.downsize shadows the first definition, causing existing 4-arg callers to silently discard the height argument and produce wrong-sized images

adjudication.rationale: In `optimized_image.rb`, `self.downsize` is defined twice: first as `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and later again as `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby, the later definition overwrites the former, so existing callers passing 4–5 arguments (width, height, opts) will hit the new 3–4 arg signature, causing arity errors (for 5 args) or misbinding `opts` (e.g., `opts` becomes an Integer) leading to runtime errors when accessing `opts[:allow_animation]`. This is a real, diff-verifiable defect caused by the duplicate method definition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In-place downsize loop overwrites the user's original upload with no backup, potentially permanently destroying the only copy of the uploaded file if conversion fails partway

adjudication.rationale: The new loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, using the same path for input and output. There is no backup copy and the return value isn’t checked, so if `downsize/convert_with` fails or writes a partial file, the only server-side copy (`tempfile`) can be corrupted before `Upload.create_for` runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No lower bound on the downsize loop: tempfile.size can stay above max_image_size_kb after 5 attempts and Upload.create_for still runs, failing size validation after destroying the original

adjudication.rationale: The loop is explicitly bounded (`attempt = 5` and `while attempt > 0 ...`), so it’s not missing a bound. It’s true the file may still exceed `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` after 5 downsizes, but the diff does not show any “destroying the original” (it only rewrites the temp file path in place) nor does it show that `Upload.create_for` will necessarily fail validation in a problematic way; that behavior isn’t verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side 413 cap hardcodes 10MB in utilities.js, desynchronizing from the server's max_image_size_kb setting, causing silent rejection of allowed images or acceptance of files the server rejects

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces client-side max size checks that previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) in `utilities.js` (both the general file-size check and the 413 handler). This can diverge from the server-configured limits (`SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` / other max_* settings), causing the client to reject uploads that the server would allow when the setting is >10MB, or allow uploads up to 10MB that the server may reject when the setting is <10MB. The server-side change in `uploads_controller.rb` also hardcodes URL download to `10.megabytes`, further desynchronizing from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FileHelper.is_image?(filename) misclassifies when filename is a URL basename

adjudication.rationale: The new auto-downsize block in `UploadsController#create_upload` is gated by `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` where `filename` can come from `File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)` for API URL uploads. URL path basenames can be empty or lack an extension (or otherwise not reflect the true content type), so using the basename as the sole signal for “is image?” can cause the downsizing feature to be skipped for real images. The diff doesn’t show `FileHelper.is_image?`’s implementation, so the exact misclassification can’t be proven here, but the risk is diff-grounded in the new conditional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored in uploads_controller.rb:63-69, so failed downsizes are silently swallowed with no logging of ImageMagick failures

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` (lines added around 60-69) but does not check its return value. In optimized_image.rb, `convert_with` suppresses ImageMagick output (`&> /dev/null`) and returns `false` on nonzero exit status, so a failed downsize can happen with no logging/handling; the loop will just keep trying (up to 5) and then proceed to `Upload.create_for` regardless. This is a concrete observability/edge-case gap introduced by the diff, not necessarily a functional correctness break visible from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) uses the same path for input and output, causing ImageMagick to fail or produce a corrupted image that is persisted as the upload

adjudication.rationale: The new upload logic in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, passing the same file path for both `from` and `to`. `OptimizedImage.optimize` forwards both paths into ImageMagick command instructions and `convert_with` executes them, so using identical input/output paths risks in-place overwrite/failure, potentially leaving a corrupted/failed image that is then persisted via `Upload.create_for(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side hardcoded 10 * 1024 limit in utilities.js:182 desyncs from server-side SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, causing 413 errors reporting the wrong limit

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` in `utilities.js` for both the pre-upload size check and the HTTP 413 handler, replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings[...]` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. Server-side code in `uploads_controller.rb` still references `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (e.g., the new downsizing loop), so if the site setting is not exactly 10MB, the client-side limit and the error message can diverge from the server’s effective limit, leading to incorrect client rejection or misleading “file too large” messaging on 413.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fixed 5-iteration loop with blind '80%' shrink cannot downsize very large images below max_image_size_kb, causing deterministic rejection of the largest files

adjudication.rationale: The new server-side downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` caps at 5 iterations and always applies `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)` while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. This does not guarantee the file will end up under the configured max for very large images (there exist inputs where 5×0.8 resizes still leave the file above the limit), so the stated intent in the comment (“automatically reduced to allowed size”) may not hold. However, the diff does not show the downstream rejection path (e.g., what `Upload.create_for` does when still oversized), so the “deterministic rejection” claim can’t be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Animated-GIF branch in optimized_image.rb is keyed on '.GIF' filename extension, but controller passes tempfile.path with no extension, so animated GIFs are silently flattened to a single frame and allow_animation is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In optimized_image.rb, the animated branch is selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true AND `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` (i.e., based on the source path’s filename extension). The new controller logic downsizes large images by calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. For the API URL case, the tempfile is created via `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")`, which provides a prefix without an extension, so `tempfile.path` will not end in `.gif` even if the original `filename` is a GIF. That means the `_animated` instructions won’t be used during this downsizing loop, plausibly flattening animated GIFs to a single frame when reduction occurs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: downsize is defined twice in the same module body in optimized_image.rb:139-152, with the second definition silently overriding the first

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/optimized_image.rb, the diff shows two `def self.downsize` definitions in the same class/module body: one taking `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and a later one taking `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby, the second definition silently overrides the first, so the earlier arity/signature is lost, which is a real behavior change/defect likely to break callers using the 4-argument form.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FileHelper.is_image?(filename) gates downsizing on a filename that may lack an extension for API-URL uploads, silently skipping downsizing for those files with no distinguishing log

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new downsizing block is gated by `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` (and `filename` for API URL uploads is derived solely from `File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)`). If the URL path has no extension (or a non-indicative basename), this condition can prevent downsizing even when the downloaded file is an image, potentially defeating the stated intent (“allow users to upload large images… reduced to allowed size”). The diff doesn’t show how `FileHelper.is_image?` works, so it’s an edge-case concern rather than a definitively verifiable defect.
